recorded: 2026-09-28, gfx1151 Strix Halo (zbook), Gemma 4 26B-A4B UD-Q4_K_XL, MMQ gate/up prefill divergence
summary: The recorded MMQ prefill divergence reproduces exactly on the current tree, and the padded-tail-tile hypothesis is refuted by a direct dump of the count distribution. The dump does confirm the recorded lead concretely: the scratch tile capacity is a capacity, not a live size, and it is 3-30x the work the route actually runs.

reproduction.result: all nine values match the recorded artifact to four significant figures, 7 over the 5e-2 bar, top-1 flips at 24 and 64, deterministic across repeats, route launched 58 times at every length
reproduction.environment_note: the documented probe command fails on libamdhip64.so because it runs miniforge base without the ROCm SDK libraries on LD_LIBRARY_PATH. The host needs the docs/ENVS.md clean-process wrapper with the _rocm_sdk_core and _rocm_sdk_devel lib directories prepended. This is a documentation gap, not a route defect.

distribution_dump.method: wrapped hipengine.kernels.hip_gfx1100.moe.group_scatter.qwen35_moe_mmq32_tile_map, which the route imports locally, and read back expert_start, mmq_expert_start and mmq_total after each real call; ran a single forward per length through the public path with HIPENGINE_GEMMA4_MOE_GATE_UP_MMQ=1
distribution_dump.columns: ids, compact_rows, total_padded (padded rows the leaf is launched over), experts_with_rows, experts_whose_count_is_not_a_multiple_of_32, tile_capacity
distribution_dump.tile_capacity_derivation: scratch.buffer('mmq_tile_expert').nbytes // 8, sized from total_lanes = tokens * top_k for the widest block the scratch serves: 8192 / 32 + 1 = 257. The live work is 55 to 93 tiles, so the capacity is 2.8x to 4.7x the work at these lengths and larger still at shorter ones.

refuted_this_pass.hypothesis: the padded tail tile per expert - each expert's last 32-row tile is partial unless its count is a multiple of 32, and which experts have a partial tile changes with N, which would be deterministic and non-monotonic in N.
refuted_this_pass.refuted_by: the dump. Every expert with rows has a partial tile at every length tested, including 96 ids which is exact at 1.66e-06. 82 of 82 at 64 ids, 89 of 90 at 96 ids. The property is present in both the diverging and the exact case, so it cannot be the trigger.
refuted_this_pass.also_checked: the tile map kernel qwen35_moe_wmma_tile_map_kernel in hipengine/kernels/hip_gfx1100/moe/group_scatter.hip is correct on inspection: a double-buffered Hillis-Steele inclusive scan with the read staged before a barrier, exclusive starts computed as prefix - padded, the total written at index num_experts, and every padded tile assigned to its expert. mmq_expert_start diffs match sum(ceil(count/32))*32 exactly at every length. The identity buffer in hipengine/kernels/hip_gfx1100/gemma4/gemma4_experts.py:899-905 is also correctly sized: total_lanes = tokens * top_k, the buffer is lanes * 8 bytes, and the arange is total_lanes int64.

what_the_dump_leaves: The discriminator is not any single structural property of the distribution. It correlates with raggedness: at 64 ids only 82 of 128 experts have rows and counts range 0 to 52, while the exact lengths 384, 512, 768 and 1024 have every expert populated and counts near the mean. But 96 ids is exact at 90 of 128 experts, which is still ragged, so raggedness alone is not it either.

tile_capacity being 257 against 84 to 93 live tiles is the one measured quantity that is wildly out of proportion, and it is exactly what the recorded lead said to check: whether the once-per-object map and the padded starts stay valid when the live lane count is far below the capacity. The dump establishes that the capacity is 2.8x to 4.7x the live work at these lengths; it does not yet establish that anything downstream misbehaves because of it.

The next concrete step is to read the leaf, gguf_q4_k_selected_dual_q8_1_ds4_mmq32_fused_prefill_compact32_bf16_bf16_out in hipengine/kernels/hip_gfx1100/quant/gguf_q4_k_q8_1_selected_prefill.hip, and check what it does with tile_capacity, total_rows and the identity map when the live tile count is far below capacity - in particular whether any index is derived from the capacity rather than from total_rows.
limits: Four lengths dumped, two diverging and one exact. The 16/48/128/192/256 lengths were reproduced but not dumped.
The dump reads the buffers after the launch returns, so it establishes the map's contents but not the leaf's consumption of it.
Single forward per length; the recorded determinism was confirmed by the probe's repeats, not re-measured here.
The fine-structure remeasurement used --repeats 1, so determinism was not re-confirmed at the new lengths; it was confirmed at the recorded lengths by the earlier probe run.

The gate/up capture reads the shared gate_up_out buffer after the call, so it compares the two arms' projections on identical inputs but does not separate quantization error from any indexing defect inside the leaf. Distinguishing those needs a reference computed at higher precision on the same input.
The three-plane prediction of a 1630x error reduction is a property of the PACK arithmetic and remains untested end to end, because no leaf on this route consumes more than one plane.

leaf_contract_cleared_this_pass.why: The dump left one named next step: read the leaf and check what it does with tile_capacity, total_rows and the identity map when the live tile count is far below capacity, in particular whether any index is derived from the capacity rather than from total_rows. That pass is done and it cleared the surface it was aimed at.
cleared: Grid dimension: the launcher computes row_tiles = mmq_total_rows / 32, so the grid covers every padded tile rather than only the compact rows. Correct.

Row masking inside the leaf body: valid_rows is min(expert_count - tile_row_in_expert, 32) with a <= 0 guard, and valid_route is local_route >= 0 && local_route < expert_count. Padded rows are masked at both the weight and the activation load. Correct.

Activation plane stride agreement: the pack kernel gguf_q8_1_mmq_ds4_pack_bf16_kernel writes plane_blocks = rows * blocks_per_row with rows = compact_rows, and the leaf body reads plane_blocks = q8_blocks_per_row * source_rows where the fused kernel passes source_rows = compact_rows. The two match exactly and both take the same compact_rows. No stride mismatch.

Activation indexing: source_row = compact_to_source[compact_base + local_route] with local_route bounded by expert_count, so compact_row stays inside [0, compact_rows) and the identity map is read in range.
The identity buffer itself: total_lanes = tokens * top_k, buffer is lanes * 8 bytes, arange is total_lanes int64. Correctly sized, and its contents are the identity the comment claims.
leaf_contract_cleared_this_pass.not_cleared: tile_capacity is still the one measured quantity out of proportion to the live work, and nothing in this pass showed anything misbehaving because of it. The capacity is derived from the widest block (8192 lanes / 32 + 1 = 257) while the live work is 84 to 93 tiles at the dumped lengths.

capacity_arithmetic_note.observation: tile_capacity must cover sum(ceil(count_e / 32)) tiles, which is compact_rows / 32 only when every expert's count is a multiple of 32. For a ragged distribution it approaches (compact_rows + 31 * experts_with_rows) / 32. The capacity is instead derived from total_lanes / 32 + 1, which is a different quantity: at 64 ids, total_lanes = 512 gives 17 tiles but the route actually needs 84.
capacity_arithmetic_note.why_it_did_not_bite_here: the scratch is sized for the widest block the route serves, 1024 tokens or 8192 lanes, giving 257 tiles, and the caller guards total_rows > tile_capacity * 32 before launching. At the dumped lengths 84 and 93 are both under 257, so the guard never fires and no tile is dropped.
capacity_arithmetic_note.why_it_is_still_the_lead: it is tight in the other direction. At 1024 ids the padded total is about 8192, which is 256 tiles against a capacity of 257, so a slightly more ragged distribution at the widest length would hit the guard rather than silently corrupt. A route whose capacity is 17 tiles at one length and 257 at another, sized by the widest, is exactly the 'scratch is a capacity, not an identity' shape the recorded artifact flagged, and the guard converts an overflow into a raise rather than a wrong answer - which is the right design but does not explain a wrong answer at 64 ids.
capacity_arithmetic_note.next: the trigger is still unidentified. What this pass adds is a cleared list: the tile map kernel, the identity buffer, the grid dimension, the row masking and the pack/leaf stride agreement are all correct, so the remaining surface is narrower than it was. The next step is to compare the leaf's actual per-tile inputs at 64 ids against 96 ids rather than reading more source.

tile_map_verified_well_formed.why: The recorded lead pointed at the per-length count distribution, the padded starts, and whether they stay valid when the live lane count is far below the scratch capacity. I reconstructed exactly what the leaf computes per tile from the dumped tile_expert, expert_start_compact and expert_start_mmq32, at both a diverging and an exact length.
tile_map_verified_well_formed.check: for every tile: expert_id = tile_expert[t], compact_base = expert_start_compact[e], expert_count = expert_start_compact[e+1] - compact_base, padded_base = expert_start_mmq32[e], tile_row_in_expert = t*32 - padded_base, valid_rows = clamp(expert_count - tile_row_in_expert, 0, 32); then claim compact_base + tile_row_in_expert + i for i in range(valid_rows)

result.columns: ids, compact_rows, total_padded, tiles, tile_capacity, tiles_with_bad_expert_id, rows_claimed_twice, rows_out_of_range, rows_uncovered, experts_used

tile_map_verified_well_formed.reading: the tile map is structurally perfect at every length tested, including the diverging ones. Every compact row is claimed exactly once, no tile carries a bad expert id, nothing is out of range and nothing is uncovered. This kills the whole count-distribution, padded-tile and padded-start family that the recorded lead pointed at. The capacity is still out of proportion to the live work, but nothing on this path misbehaves because of it.

fine_structure_remeasured.why: The recorded summary said the route is wrong at most lengths from 16 to 256. The recorded over-the-bar set was 16, 24, 32, 48, 64, 128, 256 with 192 at 0.003151, which is INSIDE the 5e-2 bar. So the passing set is larger than the record implies and the boundary had never been resolved finely.
fine_structure_remeasured.reading: only three of eleven lengths in 80 to 176 exceed the bar: 128, 136 and 160. The other eight pass, most of them by four to five orders of magnitude. The divergence is not a property of short prefills as a class; it is specific lengths, and 176 passes at 0.04759 only just inside the bar. The full measured picture is now PASS at 80, 88, 96, 104, 112, 120, 144, 176, 192, 384, 512, 768, 1024 and FAIL at 16, 24, 32, 48, 64, 128, 136, 160, 256.

reframing_the_question.the_new_fact: max|delta logit| has a median of 2.49 across ALL 1022 rows of the recorded 2048/1024 chain, including the 1019 rows whose KL is below 1e-3, with p95 6.61 and max 22.14 (benchmarks/results/2026-09-27-gemma4-moe-gate-up-mmq-measured-not-promoted.json, correctness.logit_perturbation). So the route perturbs logits by order 2.5 everywhere, always. The KL swing is then margin-driven: whether a 2.5-magnitude perturbation shows up as KL 1e-06 or as KL 2.036 depends on how close the decision is at that length, not on anything length-gated in the route.
reframing_the_question.why_this_matters: the question was 'why does the route break at 64 ids'. The measurement says the route is perturbing every length, and 96 ids is not a length where it works - it is a length where a 2.5-magnitude perturbation happens to be nearly softmax-invariant. That is a different defect with a different fix.
reframing_the_question.the_lead_it_points_at: a perturbation that is often softmax-invariant is a per-row constant offset, which is what a slightly wrong per-row sum or bias term produces. The DS4 pack stores one sum per 32-element sub-block in ds4[2*ds4_idx + 1] and the leaf reads it as activation_tile[...].ds[1], so a systematic error in how that sum is used is exactly the shape of a per-row constant. The recorded note that 'much of that is a softmax-invariant global shift' points the same way. This has not been tested and is the next thing to measure, not a conclusion.
reframing_the_question.not_yet_established: that the perturbation is in fact a constant offset, and that the offset comes from the stored sum. Both are hypotheses the next measurement should settle directly by comparing the MMQ and fp32 gate/up outputs at one layer for one length, rather than by reading more source.

gate_up_error_is_length_independent.why: The reframing said the route perturbs logits everywhere and the KL swing is margin-driven. That predicts the gate/up projection error itself is the same at a diverging length and an exact one. This measures it directly instead of inferring it from downstream KL.
gate_up_error_is_length_independent.method: Wrap both gate/up arms and copy the shared gate_up_out buffer after the call, so both arms are compared on the SAME layer, the SAME input and the SAME buffer at one length. Reshape to (lanes, 2*704) and compare per row.
gate_up_error_is_length_independent.finding_1_constant_offset_refuted: The perturbation is not a per-row constant. |row mean| / row std is 0.32 at both lengths rather than far above 1, the within-row range has a median of 5.0 and 6.6, and per-row std runs to 5.7. The stored-sum lead from the previous pass is dead: a per-row constant offset is not the shape of this error.
gate_up_error_is_length_independent.finding_2_the_error_is_length_independen: The gate/up error at 64 ids and at 96 ids is statistically indistinguishable - abs max 38.75 vs 38.57, abs mean 0.82 vs 0.99, row-mean median 0.464 vs 0.539, row-std median 0.604 vs 0.841, ratio 0.324 vs 0.337. Same magnitude, same structure, same spread. Yet 64 ids reports KL 2.036 and 96 ids reports 1.66e-06.
gate_up_error_is_length_independent.finding_3_the_diagnosis: The MMQ prefill route does not diverge at specific short lengths. It carries a large length-independent numerical error in the gate/up projection - mean absolute delta of order 0.8 to 1.0 and a maximum of 38.7 against bf16 outputs - at every length. The apparent length dependence is entirely a downstream decision-margin artifact of measuring a single forward's next-token KL, which is a threshold on how close the decision happens to be, not a measure of the route's error. 96 ids is not a length where the route is correct; it is a length where an unchanged 0.8-magnitude projection error happens to be nearly softmax-invariant.
gate_up_error_is_length_independent.consequence_for_the_gate: The named clearing condition is scripts/gemma4_mmq_prefill_length_probe.py exiting 0 at every length. That condition tests downstream margin, not the route's error. A route with a much smaller projection error could still fail at a length whose margin is tight, and the current route passes at lengths where the margin is loose. The condition should be restated against the gate/up projection error - for example the mean absolute delta measured here - rather than against a per-length KL threshold. This is a finding about the gate, and changing it is a separate decision from fixing the route.
gate_up_error_is_length_independent.next: Establish whether the 0.8-magnitude error is inherent to DS4 Q8_1 activation quantization at this geometry or is a defect, by comparing the fp32 arm against a high-precision reference on the same input, and by measuring the activation dynamic range the pack is quantizing. The same MMQ route is measured and promoted for Qwen35, so the question is what differs about Gemma4's activations - dynamic range and outlier structure are the candidates - rather than whether int8 can work at all.

root_cause_is_the_quantization_budget_no.why: Task 15 asked whether the ~0.8 mean absolute gate/up error is inherent to DS4 Q8_1 activation quantization or a defect in the leaf. This settles it by construction rather than by argument: run the FP32 arm on activations that have merely been quantized to DS4 and back, and compare that delta against the MMQ arm's delta. The fp32 arm has no MMQ leaf in it at all, so whatever error it shows on quantized activations is the quantization budget and nothing else.
root_cause_is_the_quantization_budget_no.method: At one layer, one length, three runs on the same input: (A) fp32 arm on the real activations; (B) fp32 arm with packed_hidden replaced in place by its DS4 round-trip, computed in numpy exactly as the pack kernel does it - scale = max|v|/127 per 32-element sub-block, q = clamp(rint(v/scale), -127, 127), stored scale rounded to fp16, v_hat = q * fp16(scale); (C) the MMQ arm on the real activations. The pack's own arithmetic is read from gguf_q8_1_mmq_ds4_pack_bf16_kernel, so the simulation matches the kernel line for line.
root_cause_is_the_quantization_budget_no.conclusion: The MMQ route's entire gate/up error IS the DS4 activation quantization budget. The fp32 arm on activations that have only been quantized and dequantized reproduces the MMQ arm's error to four significant figures - max 38.7500 against 38.7500 and mean 0.8225 against 0.8226 at 64 ids, and 38.5635 against 38.5703 and 0.9905 against 0.9904 at 96 ids - at a ratio of 1.00x at both lengths. There is no leaf defect. The route implements DS4 Q8_1 activation quantization correctly, and the residual against the fp32 arm is exactly what quantizing the activation to int8 with a per-32 scale costs.
root_cause_is_the_quantization_budget_no.why_this_is_the_floor: The activation dynamic range is modest, not pathological: the per-sub-block max over median ratio is 5.1 to 5.2, so the outlier structure the previous task named as a candidate is not the problem. The round-trip relative error is 0.717 percent rms, and with a max over median of about 5 that is at the practical floor for int8 with one scale per 32 elements - the step is max|v|/254, so the relative error is roughly the outlier ratio over 254. A better scale search, a different outlier handling or a wider sub-block would not move it much. Getting materially below this needs more than 8 bits per activation, not a repaired leaf.
root_cause_is_the_quantization_budget_no.consequence: The route cannot be fixed by repairing the leaf, because the leaf is not wrong. The named clearing condition - the length probe exiting 0 - is testing the model's sensitivity to a 0.717 percent perturbation of the gate/up activation, and no amount of correctness work on the MMQ route changes that number. The route is therefore at its correctness ceiling for this activation format, and the choice is between accepting the perturbation, raising activation precision, and not using this route.
root_cause_is_the_quantization_budget_no.candidate_lever_not_yet_tested: The pack kernel takes residual_passes as a template parameter and the leaf already indexes its activation planes by activation_pass, so multi-pass packing with error feedback - residual = residual - q * scale, which the pack already computes - is a supported shape that would cut the quantization error without changing the activation format. Whether the gate/up route is instantiated with more than one pass is not established here and is the cheapest next thing to check. It is named as a candidate, not a recommendation.
limits: The comparison uses numpy to reproduce the pack arithmetic; it matched the kernel to four significant figures at both lengths, which is strong evidence the simulation is faithful, but it is a simulation of the pack rather than the pack itself.
Only one layer, the first, was compared. Nothing here says the error is uniform across layers.

The fp32 arm is treated as the reference. Task 14 established it is bit-identical to the strict single-kernel arm on both chains, so it is a sound reference, but it is not an independently-computed high-precision reference.

task15_answer.question: Is the ~0.8 mean absolute MMQ gate/up error inherent to DS4 Q8_1 activation quantization at this geometry, or a defect in the leaf? And since the identical route is measured and promoted for Qwen35, what differs about Gemma4's activations?
task15_answer.answer: The error is inherent to activation quantization and the leaf is correct - but it is NOT a property of Gemma4's activations. Nothing differs about Gemma4's activations. What differs is the route's ACTIVATION PACKING PRECISION: the Gemma4 route packs ONE activation plane, while the Qwen35 route packs THREE with error feedback (the d4x3 shape). Single-plane packing costs 0.717 percent relative activation error, which is the entire 0.8 mean absolute gate/up error, and it is the one thing the Gemma4 route does differently.
task15_answer.evidence_1_the_leaf_is_correct: Running the fp32 arm on activations that had only been quantized to DS4 and back reproduces the MMQ arm's error to four significant figures - at 64 ids max 38.7500 vs 38.7500 and mean 0.8225 vs 0.8226, at 96 ids 38.5635 vs 38.5703 and 0.9905 vs 0.9904 - at a ratio of 1.00x at both lengths. The fp32 arm contains no MMQ leaf, so there is nothing left for a leaf defect to explain.
task15_answer.evidence_2_the_range_is_not_the_problem: The activation dynamic range is modest: per-32-element-sub-block max over median is 5.14 at 64 ids and 5.22 at 96 ids, activation rms 0.289 and 0.277, max abs 3.36 at both. The outlier structure that the task named as a leading candidate is not present. 0.717 percent rms is the practical floor for int8 with one scale per 32 elements, since the step is max|v|/254 and the relative error is roughly the outlier ratio over 254.
task15_answer.evidence_3_the_packing_precision_is_the_: gemma4_experts.py sizes mmq_workspace as lanes * (hidden_size // 128) * 144 with the comment 'the size the single-plane pack kernel writes'. A DS4 block is 144 bytes, so that is exactly ONE activation plane, and the Gemma4 route therefore runs the one-pass pack. The same file family exports hipengine_gguf_q8_1_mmq_ds4_pack_bf16_d4x3 for three passes, and qwen4_exp_profiles.py names d4x3 variants throughout. The pack kernel's own error feedback - residual = residual - q * scale, which it already computes on every pass - is what makes the extra planes worth their bytes.

evidence_4_the_predicted_fix.method: reproduced the pack's multi-pass arithmetic in numpy on the real captured Gemma4 activations, 512 rows x 2816 hidden, 45056 sub-blocks of 32
evidence_4_the_predicted_fix.reading: two planes cut the activation error 257x and three planes cut it 1630x. Since the measured gate/up error is exactly the one-plane quantization budget, three-plane packing predicts a gate/up error of about 0.0005 mean and 0.024 max instead of 0.8226 and 38.75.

task15_answer.the_fix_is_already_built: A three-pass MMQ32 prefill leaf is already exported: hipengine_gguf_q4_k_t16_selected_dual_q8_1_ds4x3_mmq32_prefill_compact32_bf16_bf16_out. So the change is to size mmq_workspace for three planes, call the d4x3 pack, and launch the ds4x3 leaf - not to write a kernel.
what_this_does_not_establish: The 1630x figure is a prediction from the pack arithmetic, not a measurement of the three-plane route. The gate/up error after the change must be measured, not assumed.

It does not establish that three-plane packing clears the KL bar at every length. It predicts the projection error falls far enough that it should, but the bar is a downstream margin and task 14 showed that margin is what the probe measures.

It does not establish the cost. Three planes mean three times the activation bytes and three times the pack work, which eats into the 1.265x the route is measured to win by. That must be measured before any promotion.

why_three_planes_did_not_work.correction: The task-15 note said the three-plane fix was already built and the change was 'three edits'. That was wrong, and the measurement is what showed it. The three-pass leaf that exists is not a three-pass leaf for this route's activation format.
why_three_planes_did_not_work.the_actual_blocker: The DS4 MMQ prefill body reads its activations with no pass term at all. Every DS4 activation read is x_q8[q8_block] where q8_block = compact_row * q8_mmq_blocks_per_row + blk * 2 + (sb >> 2) - see gguf_q4_k_q8_1_selected_prefill.hip lines 1755, 1786, 1892, 1923, 2029, 2060, 2163, 2191, 2318, 2346, 2476, 2504. There is no static_cast<int64_t>(pass) * plane_blocks term anywhere in the DS4 path. The only sites that carry a pass offset are the block_q8_1_mmq_ds4_f32 ones (lines 3548, 3623, 3655, 4323, 4340, 4397, 4456, 4481, 4597), which are a different block type and a different body.
why_three_planes_did_not_work.what_the_working_route_uses: The only three-pass MMQ leaves in the file are the _ds4x3_f32_ T16 mmq64x32 variants - hipengine_gguf_q4_k_t16_selected_dual_q8_1_ds4x3_f32_mmq64x32_prefill_compact32_bf16_bf16_out and its q6_k siblings. They use block_q8_1_mmq_ds4_f32, whose ds header is eight floats rather than eight uint16, and that is the family qwen4_exp_profiles.py names throughout. So Qwen35's working d4x3 route is the f32-activation family with three planes, and the Gemma 4 route is the f16-activation family with one plane.
why_three_planes_did_not_work.so_the_difference_is: Not the activation values, and not the leaf being wrong. It is that Gemma 4's route is on the f16 DS4 activation family, which has no multi-pass code path, while the promoted Qwen35 route is on the f32 DS4 activation family, which does.
why_three_planes_did_not_work.what_fixing_it_actually_requires: One of two things, neither of which is three edits. (a) Add a pass loop to the DS4 (f16) WMMA body. That is a real kernel change and it has a subtlety: the inner loop accumulates an int8xint4 dot product into dot_acc and then applies acc_f[j] += scale_f * xd * dot_acc[j] - min_f * xsum, so a pass loop has to decide how the min_f * xsum correction composes across planes rather than simply adding another dot product. The f32 body is the reference for how that is done. (b) Move the Gemma 4 route to the f32 activation family, which needs a fused RAW f32 leaf that does not exist yet. Either way this is a kernel unit with its own correctness gate, not a configuration flip.
why_three_planes_did_not_work.state_landed: The kernel-level enabler is landed and correct: the fused leaf kernel is now templated on ACTIVATION_PASSES instead of hardcoding 1, the launcher forwards it, and hipengine_gguf_q4_k_selected_dual_q8_1_ds4x3_fused_mmq32_prefill_compact32_bf16_bf16_out is exported. The route stays on one plane, because with the body reading one plane a three-plane pack would pay three times the activation bytes and pack work for no accuracy.
why_three_planes_did_not_work.measured: With three populated activation planes, the workspace sized for three, the launcher forwarding ACTIVATION_PASSES = 3 and the route instrumented to confirm it calls the new ds4x3 symbol, the gate/up error is bit-identical: mean absolute 0.8225 at 64 ids against 0.8225 for the one-plane quantization arm, ratio 1.00x.

task18_premises_corrected.why: Before restructuring a hot inner loop in ~12 places, I tried to verify the payoff and the mechanism. Both checks changed the plan, and one of them refutes an assumption I recorded in the task-16 note.

finding_1_the_harness_cannot_measure_the.what_i_did: Quantized packed_hidden to 1, 2 and 3 planes, reconstructed it exactly as the leaf would (sum_p q_p * scale_p), wrote it back into the activation buffer and ran the real fp32 grouped route, so the delta against the unmodified fp32 run is the error the MMQ route would carry at that plane count. No kernel change involved.
finding_1_the_harness_cannot_measure_the.reading: The error is identical at one, two and three planes, which is NOT evidence that the fix cannot work. It is a harness artifact: the activation buffer is bf16 by construction, so the reconstruction is rounded to an 8-bit mantissa on the way back in, and that rounding (about 0.2 percent relative) dominates the three-plane reconstruction error (0.00044 percent). The one-plane DS4 error (0.717 percent) still dominates bf16 rounding, which is why the one-plane number agrees with the MMQ route. So this method can measure the one-plane error and cannot measure the multi-plane one.
finding_1_the_harness_cannot_measure_the.consequence: The task-18 payoff remains UNVERIFIED. The prediction that the gate/up error falls about 1630x with three planes follows from the projection being linear in the activation error, and that linearity has not been tested. The kernel change is the only way to measure it, because the leaf consumes int8 directly and never round-trips through bf16.

finding_2_the_sum_correction_does_not_te.the_assumption_i_recorded: The task-16 note said the per-pass sums telescope, so a pass loop could simply accumulate the stored xsum values: sum_p sum(residual_p) approximately equals the reconstruction's own sum.
finding_2_the_sum_correction_does_not_te.measurement: It does not. |sum_p sum(residual_p) - sum of the reconstruction| over |mean reconstruction sum| is 5.84e-02 at 64 ids and 6.12e-02 at 96 ids - about six percent, not negligible. The extra term sum_p sum(residual_{p+1}) is comparable in size to the reconstruction sum rather than small.
finding_2_the_sum_correction_does_not_te.so_a_pass_loop_must_not: accumulate the stored ds4[2*ds4_idx + 1] values across passes. That would introduce a several-percent error in the min_f * xsum correction term, which is exactly the kind of error this work exists to remove.
finding_2_the_sum_correction_does_not_te.what_the_working_reference_does: The f32 multi-pass body does not use the stored sum at all. At lines 4473 onward it reads the per-pass block, takes d = ds4[2*(k32&3)] as the per-pass scale, and computes sum0/sum1 by dp4a-summing the int8 qs bytes directly with gguf_q4_k_mmq_dp4a(0x01010101u, ...). So the effective activation sum is d_p * sum(q_p) accumulated across passes, which does converge to sum(x), rather than sum(residual_p) accumulated across passes, which does not.
finding_2_the_sum_correction_does_not_te.the_even_simpler_option_the_ds4_path_has: For the DS4 block, pass 0's stored sum is sum(residual_0) = sum(x) exactly, and sum(x) is precisely what the Q4_K min-offset correction needs, since that term accounts for w_min * sum_k x[k]. So a DS4 pass loop can take the correction from pass 0 alone and accumulate only the dot products. That is cheaper than recomputing sum(q_p) per pass and is exact rather than convergent. It is a design choice for the implementer, not a measured result.

task18_premises_corrected.finding_3_the_staging_shape: The f32 body stages every pass into activation_tile[pass][row_offset] before the accumulation, so the DS4 path needs the same staging plus a per-pass accumulation of the dot product, since the per-pass scale xd differs and the int dot cannot be scaled once at the end. That is the restructure: currently one dot_acc is accumulated over kt and then scaled by a single xd inside the j loop, and multi-pass needs a separate dot_acc per pass combined with that pass's xd.
limits: The linearity of the gate/up error in the activation error is assumed, not measured. Finding 1 explains why the obvious harness cannot measure it.
Only the first layer was instrumented, as in the earlier passes.
The f32 reference was read, not run; its pass accumulation is inferred from its source at lines 4473 onward rather than from a measurement of that kernel.
